newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah unfazed by rate cut.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah unfazed by rate cut.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable after the central bank cut a key discount rate early on Wednesday, dealers said.
"The cut surprised the market but many operators had already expected the discount rate cut to take place in February or March after a cut in December," a state bank dealer in Jakarta said.

Bank Indonesia cut its key discount rates for short-term securities (SBPUs) by 50 basis points for all maturities. SBPUs are papers purchased by the central bank to inject liquidity into the banking system.
A Bank Indonesia official said the rate cut was based on the country's improved inflation outlook and there was no change in its rupiah depreciation policy.
C. Harinowo, director of the money market department, told Reuters the central bank would monitor the impact of Wednesday's rate cut before deciding whether to ease again.
MMS International said in a daily market commentary that Bank Indonesia was likely to steadily lower rates as long as there were no signs of sudden outflows of funds or a resurgence in inflation.

In Thailand, the baht continued to enjoy a period of respite as worries about the country's finance sector crisis slipped into the background, leaving the Thai unit to track the dollar/majors in subdued dealings.
The baht was quoted at 25.950-25.955 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against 25.950/25.953 late on Tuesday, as the dollar rose against the yen.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.94 per dollar against 25.93 on Tuesday.

"Flow-wise, it's been pretty quiet. It's going to trade a 25.94-25.96 range for a while but I don't think the baht's troubles are over. I still see more dollar/baht upside," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore.
The overnight interbank rate edged up to 8.50-9.00 percent in early trade as some banks started borrowing funds ahead of the central bank's reserve deadline on March 22, dealers said.

The Malaysian ringgit held on to its overnight gains but was capped near 2.4700 to the dollar as orders from importers and Kuala Lumpur banks formed a base for the U.S. unit near that level, dealers said.

"There is strong chart support (for the dollar) at 2.4685 so the market is not keen on testing that at the moment," said a Japanese bank dealer in Singapore. "For today, 2.4700 may be difficult to crack."
The ringgit was quoted at 2.4714/24 to the dollar at 0425 GMT against 2.4748/58 at its Kuala Lumpur close on Tuesday.
Dealers said the ringgit was still being bought up against the Singapore dollar and the cross looked set to reach the 0.5800 target in the near term. It was at 0.5791/98 at 0425 GMT.
But they said the Singapore dollar's downside against the U.S. dollar was being cushioned by corporate demand for the Singapore unit around S$1.4330/40.

"Dollar/yen hasn't been making a lot of headway so there's no compelling reason to take dollar/Sing higher. But I would see S$1.4340 as a short-term resistance," said the U.S. bank dealer, adding that a breach of that level would put it on track for S$1.4500.
-- Reme Ahmad in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
